lessons.root_cause: Two observer regression modules imported checkout-only scripts as installed packages. Local python -m pytest added the checkout root, masking collection errors in the hosted pytest console entrypoint.
lessons.prevention: Load reviewed script modules by exact checkout path and execute a clean subprocess regression using the actual pytest console entrypoint with PYTHONPATH removed.

lessons.root_cause: A private host-owned file is not readable by container UID 10001 under Docker rootless UID remapping.
lessons.prevention: Keep the key in a Boca-only volume and prove ownership, mode and actual UID 10001 read access before starting.

lessons.root_cause: A successful release run did not prove that the operator-supplied digest was the image scanned and published in that run.
lessons.prevention: Bind the exact digest, source SHA and first-attempt run ID to the uploaded release manifest before host credentials.

lessons.root_cause: A socket checked from UID 1000 could appear absent when it was merely inaccessible; staging capacity omitted the rootless image store.
lessons.prevention: Inspect from the dedicated UID and check both staging and validated DockerRootDir capacity before any Boca mutation.

lessons.root_cause: Configured Compose and HostConfig limits did not prove the running controller had only the Boca network, safe flags and effective rootless cgroup limits.
lessons.prevention: Inspect the attached network by exact ID, require Boca Compose labels and no foreign peers, verify security metadata, and read effective cgroup v2 limits with a fixed in-container probe before PASS.

lessons.root_cause: Initial capacity could pass before an image pull consumed rootless Docker headroom, so key creation and startup were not gated by the post-pull reserve.
lessons.prevention: Measure staging and verified Docker storage after pull and before key, then again before PASS; reject changed backend, directory or filesystem identity.

lessons.root_cause: Two fresh manual release dispatches for one SHA both had attempt 1 and could serially repush the mutable SHA tag.
lessons.prevention: Require only the current first-attempt run in bounded workflow history before build and again before registry login.

lessons.root_cause: The host workflow used deployment readiness before distinguishing read-only inspection from installation, so enabling observation also unlocked the initial install gate.
lessons.prevention: Require an independent read-only environment marker and execute the first-step operation matrix before checkout or SSH, retaining a separate deployment marker for installation.

lessons.root_cause: OpenSSH joined locally quoted command arguments into a remote shell string, losing the empty image positional argument before the host parser.
lessons.prevention: Serialize read-only remote commands with shlex.join and execute actual workflow steps through a local remote-shell transport regression.

lessons.root_cause: An absent dedicated rootless socket did not distinguish unavailable Docker executables from a missing, inactive or failed user service.
lessons.prevention: Inspect fixed executable availability and allowlisted user-service properties without daemon operations; require the dedicated identity and a proven private bus before contacting systemd.

lessons.root_cause: Unrelated pull requests and manual host operations shared a GitHub concurrency group, allowing newer pending work to replace older validation even with cancel-in-progress disabled.
lessons.prevention: Separate validation groups by pull-request number, retain one constant manual host mutex, and reject changed routing, cancellation or deployment triggers in policy and regressions.

lessons.root_cause: Database.migrate enabled WAL and ran schema DDL before validating an existing migration checksum, altering rejected databases and adopting unversioned files.
lessons.prevention: Validate the existing ledger through mode=ro, then recheck checksum and file identity through mode=rw before application DDL/WAL/chmod; reject unknown files and create fresh files exclusively.

lessons.root_cause: A double-slash anchor retained by pathlib did not match the single-slash traversal path, bypassing the candidate directory ownership and writable-mode check in a review candidate.
lessons.prevention: Require single-root absolute candidate and anchor paths, reject double-slash account homes, and keep descriptor-based no-symlink traversal with explicit ownership checks.

lessons.root_cause: The read-only local status projection enumerated schema versions only through 6 and capped ledger reads at 7, so reviewed Telegram migration 7 caused a false availability failure.
lessons.prevention: Validate each installed reviewed migration by exact checksum and set the bounded ledger query to the number of recognized versions plus one, rejecting future versions and corruption.

lessons.root_cause: The panel discarded the durable host's canonical command ID after member/event deduplication and redirected to the newly submitted operation UUID, which had no detail row.
lessons.prevention: Validate and retain the returned canonical UUID for the redirect and its replay; fail closed without a Location header if the host result has no valid command ID.

lessons.root_cause: The stop-test inventory allowlist predated the optional Telegram service, so a future valid worker would prevent Boca test shutdown as an unknown container.
lessons.prevention: Require complete inventory validation and prove the worker's fixed Compose identity, command, UID, immutable Boca image digest, local image ID and revision before any stop.

lessons.root_cause: The Site owner-volume custody preflight filtered only Boca-labeled and Boca-named containers, allowing a foreign container in the dedicated rootless daemon to remain invisible before pull or sealed bootstrap effects.
lessons.prevention: Require an empty full rootless daemon container inventory before pull, after pull, before owner directory preparation, immediately before the sealed Site helper and before reporting PASS; preserve all resources on uncertainty.

lessons.root_cause: The tablet-local owner ceremony requested residentKey preferred without a platform authenticator, so enrollment could accept a device-bound nondiscoverable credential instead of a key stored by the tablet credential manager.
lessons.prevention: Require a platform authenticator and discoverable credential with user verification in the served creation options, and explain that browser cookies hold only temporary panel sessions.

lessons.root_cause: The protected BETA failure branch stopped its controller but retained disposable Compose, container, private network and image artifacts, blocking a clean new-only preflight.
lessons.prevention: Immediately invoke bounded rootless Boca-only cleanup after a marked failed BETA stage; prove exact identities, preserve persistent volumes, and fail closed on ambiguous partial deletion.

lessons.root_cause: The first one-use owner enrollment host smoke used only a Docker --internal bridge, which has no gateway for published ports: the container stayed running while localhost:8443 refused every connection.
lessons.prevention: Use an exclusive Boca bridge with IP masquerading and intercontainer traffic disabled, bind only host loopback, verify effective NetworkSettings.Ports as well as PortBindings, and require Docker Engine 28+ before protected activation.

lessons.root_cause: The synthetic Chromium adapter accepted its fake success before async page context teardown; a context manager swallowing cancellation during __aexit__ could return success after close, STOP or deadline expiration.
lessons.prevention: Do not accept synthetic success until after context exit; recheck the deadline, closed state and pending external task cancellation before returning, even when teardown swallows CancelledError.

lessons.root_cause: The isolated synthetic AF_UNIX worker could wait indefinitely for an active handler during STOP, while client or worker teardown could still permit a late success reply after cancellation.
lessons.prevention: Cancel and fence active IPC work before bounded server shutdown, reject uncooperative socket teardown, and recheck close, cancellation and deadline after cleanup and before any synthetic success.

lessons.root_cause: The one-GET login observer treated unstyled visible controls as sufficient even after blocking external CSS, and overlooked scripts, inline on* event handlers and aria-hidden ancestors that can change or conceal the initial form.
lessons.prevention: Reject success for any aborted display asset, script/style declaration, generic on* attribute name or aria-hidden/inert ancestor; preserve offline real-Chromium SSR/CSR/CSS/hydration fixtures with no network and a fixed sanitized receipt.

lessons.root_cause: Owner enrollment stopped the dedicated daemon, browser installation did not resume it, and the legacy stop and acceptance inventory rejected the integrated browser topology or accepted a controller through legacy identity checks.
lessons.prevention: Recheck current main before guarded start, validate the complete exact installed topology before every stop or resume, and perform marked attempt cleanup on both failure and cancellation.

lessons.root_cause: The durable Telegram worker lacked an identity-bound prior API acceptance gate and a protected start path compatible with the installed browser topology; attempted sender cleanup also depended on unrelated base-service health.
lessons.prevention: Require the exact private configuration and acceptance fence before claims; validate the installed pair and new sender attempt separately, then clean only positively identified new residues without depending on base-service health.

lessons.root_cause: Real Docker Compose inspection canonicalized the sole SYS_CHROOT capability to CAP_SYS_CHROOT; postflight, stop and selective worker cleanup incorrectly rejected this equivalent representation.
lessons.prevention: Accept exactly either one-element capability spelling in the three inspect predicates; keep all other security checks and reject extra, duplicate, mixed, differently cased or non-list representations.

lessons.root_cause: SO_PEERCRED reports PID zero for an authenticated peer in a sibling PID namespace. Requiring a positive visible PID rejected the real isolated worker despite its exact kernel UID and GID.
lessons.prevention: Accept namespace-invisible PID zero only with exact kernel UID and GID, preserve socket ownership and inode checks, reject malformed or unavailable credentials, and exercise IPC across real containers before and after restart without sharing namespaces.

lessons.root_cause: The Telegram storage gate required contiguous migrations 1 through 6, but real BETA initialization creates 1, 2, 3, 5 and 6. Migration 4 belongs to optional credential-key rotation, and the old synthetic fixture hid the contract mismatch.
lessons.prevention: Validate the exact required BETA migration set with optional version 4 and phase-specific version 7, verify every checksum by its actual version, and exercise additive idempotent Telegram migration from the real initializer while preserving data, keys and delivery fences.

lessons.root_cause: The browser host gate subtracted one-minute load average from the SSH process CPU affinity, treating runnable and I/O-wait task counts as idle CPU. A two-CPU full topology was falsely rejected for any positive load, while ancestor quotas and container-branch cpusets were ignored.
lessons.prevention: Resolve the dedicated rootless systemd container branch and applicable ancestor quotas/cpusets, use the verified configured CPU ceiling with unchanged numerical thresholds, and report load only as advisory; unknown identity or controls remain NO_GO.

lessons.root_cause: The private rootless configuration reader opened an input with O_RDONLY before checking its file type, so a FIFO without a writer blocked instead of failing closed.
lessons.prevention: Open with O_NONBLOCK and O_NOFOLLOW, require one-link regular private files, and revalidate descriptor identity, links and timestamps after bounded reads; preserve unexpected filesystem entries.

lessons.root_cause: The new public capture renderer could retain provisional DOM success after late Chromium cleanup failed, while awaiting text inside any() created an async generator and broke the positive DOM gate.
lessons.prevention: Commit DOM success only after all context, browser and Playwright cleanup succeeds; await challenge text before a synchronous predicate and exercise the complete positive and late-failure adapter paths without network.

lessons.root_cause: The offline renderer stopped safely on a resource outside its capture map but omitted the rejected identity. Later STOP cancellations could also overflow the supervisor decision-count bound and discard the causal diagnostic.
lessons.prevention: Emit strictly sanitized and revalidated causal metadata within eight items/4096 bytes. Separate bounded post-STOP cancellations from evaluated requests, preserve the first cause through abort/close failures, and retain all network and request limits.

lessons.root_cause: Valid enrollment public keys and opaque owner subjects may begin with a hyphen. Callers omitted the argparse option terminator, causing exit2 before serving or executing a phase. The failed hosted run did not preserve its key; its linkage remains inferred.
lessons.prevention: Keep reviewed flags before an explicit terminator and owner operands afterward in smoke, SSH transport and container commands. Selective cleanup recognizes only exact legacy or terminated enrollment argv and preserves unproved resources.

lessons.root_cause: An HTTP owner test searched the entire randomized encrypted JSON for the substring tls. A valid base64url salt or ciphertext can contain those bytes without transporting TLS material, so the assertion caused nondeterministic false failures.
lessons.prevention: Validate the exact envelope schema and real decrypted bundle instead of searching opaque cryptographic encodings. Exercise a deterministic valid salt containing tls, retain ordinary random coverage, and prove rejection of TLS artifacts and private DER material.

lessons.root_cause: The infrastructure preflight discarded the controlled host error stream and failed to retain an exit category, hiding why its initial stopped-boundary check failed before any daemon-start attempt. The specific historical host cause remains unknown.
lessons.prevention: Capture bounded private streams, publish only exact SHA-bound receipts and allowlisted fixed reasons, keep unknown transport failures indeterminate, and provide an explicit read-only inspection that cannot enter effect or restore steps.

lessons.root_cause: The effective-unit check required display rows for empty Exec arrays, but the official systemd renderer omits those rows even with --all. A valid seven-row response was rejected before daemon start. The exact historical host output was not retained.
lessons.prevention: Keep six strict scalar properties and require six explicit typed Properties.Get results with exact signature, five empty hooks and one canonical argv vector. Missing properties, malformed output, command drift and read failures remain NO_GO without side effects or raw diagnostics.

lessons.root_cause: Unbenchmarked preventive host RAM/CPU/PID buffers were enforced as a predeploy admission veto, though no complete Boca BETA consumption measurement existed. Run #290 failed at its observation step; public logs do not establish which concrete metric triggered it.
lessons.prevention: Keep exact advisory predeploy observations, not unbenchmarked admission vetoes. Preserve rootless identity, port 8443 isolation, cgroup caps, storage safety, SHA/digest provenance and selective cleanup. Measure actual BETA resource use and latency after installation.

lessons.root_cause: The protected owner-enroll start step discarded remote stderr and converted all failed host starts to a generic NO_GO, hiding the failing stage in real runs #305 and #306.
lessons.prevention: Report only fixed host-owned start phase codes via a bounded ephemeral runner file; forbid raw stderr, retain the failed result and always perform Boca-only cleanup and daemon stop.

lessons.root_cause: Two workflows shared the same GitHub Releases Trivy installer. Three hosted attempts ended with curl-compatible exit code 6 after resolving v0.76.1 but before scanning; the failed hostname is unknown.
lessons.prevention: Use the publisher's immutable OCI Trivy 0.76.1 on hosted runners for all six scans. Require exact local SHA and Docker-only source, unchanged HIGH/CRITICAL OS/library coverage including unfixed CVEs, and fail closed on scan or network error.

lessons.root_cause: The beta-install helper still required 768 MiB MemAvailable and 0.5 CPU at each inventory despite approved advisory policy; acceptance also required 512 MiB/0.25 CPU. In protected run 41890280818 an earlier PASS became beta-apply NO_GO with no final memory value.
lessons.prevention: Record valid host RAM/CPU observations rather than unbenchmarked vetoes. Reject invalid metadata; preserve rootless identity, hard cgroups, SHA, storage, network and Boca-only cleanup. Measure real consumption in protected synthetic acceptance.

lessons.root_cause: The genuine historical controller image from release 41893887078 lacks org.opencontainers.image.source. Cutover A retires its final container before generic cleanup; after COMMITTED, the unreferenced GHCR image becomes unverified/INDETERMINATE (or may be missed by digest-only reference filters) and prevents terminal ACCEPT despite an accepted candidate.
lessons.prevention: Before irreversible retirement, bind exact legacy container Image ID to the independently verified historical GHCR RepoDigest and revision SHA with field-only inspection, reject any foreign alias and existing uncertain Boca residue, then reattest only this exact image on every cleanup probe and delete by immutable ID with global ID-only absence proof. Preserve all other unknowns, active references and foreign workloads; never prune or force-remove.

lessons.root_cause: PREPARE #42073058087 returned exit 3 without stderr. The real observer reused cleanup._inspect_field, whose cleanup-only allowlist excludes required Config.Image, HostConfig.*, State.Health.Status and volume Mountpoint. FakeIO tests missed the adapter; first host error remains unproven.
lessons.prevention: Use exact read-only Docker field projection for the production observer (UID/GID10001), separate from cleanup. Validate SHA64 container IDs and exact Boca volume; deny Config.Env and foreign fields. Test the real adapter deterministically before new protected PREPARE.
